newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends slightly higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends slightly higher in thin trade.

text.p: COMEX copper nudged barely higher by close after a choppy, nervous session with no news to give the market direction.
Traders were waiting for Tuesday's LME stock report. Stocks unexpectedly fell last Friday.

"It seems the market is still uneasy. The interest rates outlook is a depressant -- when they think interest rates are going to go higher, it makes the market uneasy," said Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities.
December COMEX settled 0.05 cent firmer at 89.85 cents a lb, traded from 90.80 to 89.30 cents. Spot September ended 0.05 cent firmer at 90.50 cents.
Volume was an estimated 4,000 lots an hour before close of trade.
LME three-months copper closed on the kerb down $6 a tonne from Friday with the market left drifting.
